title: AD Replication Topology Explorer
summary: Interactive topology map of DCs, sites, and intrasite/intersite replication links with clickable link health status.
teaching_value: Lets a learner click any DC-to-DC link to see simulated repadmin /showrepl output for that link (healthy, warning, or failed with the matching Event ID), directly connecting the abstract topology concept to the diagnostic command output covered in OSB-AD-LESSON-0001 and OSB-AD-LAB-0001.
elements: DCs as nodes within each site
Intrasite links styled solid (notify-driven), intersite links styled dashed (schedule-driven)
Click-to-inspect panel showing simulated repadmin output per link
rejected_if: A purely decorative animated graph with no per-link inspection would not meet the bar - flagged explicitly against that failure mode.

title: Kerberos Ticket Flow Sequence Animation
summary: Step-through animation of AS-REQ/AS-REP/TGS-REQ/TGS-REP/AP-REQ/AP-REP between client, KDC, and target service.
teaching_value: Makes the abstract ticket-granting-ticket vs service-ticket distinction concrete by animating exactly which message crosses which line, then overlays where each documented failure (KRB_AP_ERR_SKEW, KRB_AP_ERR_MODIFIED) actually breaks the sequence.
elements: Three lanes: Client, KDC, Target Service
Numbered message steps: AS-REQ, AS-REP (ticket-granting ticket issued), TGS-REQ, TGS-REP (service ticket issued), AP-REQ, AP-REP
Failure-injection toggle showing where KRB_AP_ERR_SKEW and KRB_AP_ERR_MODIFIED occur in the sequence
rejected_if: An animation that only shows 'client talks to server' without the KDC's distinct AS and TGS exchanges would not convey the actual protocol and was rejected as insufficiently specific.

title: Forest Recovery Decision Tree
summary: Decision tree from 'multiple DCs failing' through to 'contained incident' vs 'forest-wide recovery' with the branch logic from OSB-AD-TS-0003.
teaching_value: Gives learners a fast visual reference for the exact judgment call in OSB-AD-TS-0003 - shared infrastructure cause with healthy DCs elsewhere versus an actively spreading forest-wide failure - which is otherwise easy to get wrong under incident pressure.
elements: Branch: shared isolated infra cause + other DCs healthy -> Contained incident path (individual rebuild/restore)
Branch: spreading malicious/corrupting change or total inability to process changes -> Forest-wide path (full recovery guide, Microsoft Support engagement)
Terminal nodes link directly to OSB-AD-LAB-0003 for the forest-wide path and to the standard DC rebuild guidance for the contained path
rejected_if: A tree that omits the 'confirm it's actually forest-wide before acting' gate would risk teaching learners to over-trigger full forest recovery, which the underlying troubleshooting record explicitly warns against.
